theorems.name: Brownian Motion as a Scaling Limit of Random Walks
theorems.statement: For a symmetric random walk S_n rescaled as W_n(t)=S_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}/\sqrt n, W_n(t) \to B(t) in distribution as n\to\infty.
theorems.conditions: Steps must be i.i.d. mean-zero, finite variance.
theorems.intuition: Dividing by sqrt(n) normalizes the variance to match Brownian motion's unit-time variance.
theorems.proofSketch: Central Limit Theorem applied at each fixed t, plus tightness of the process.
theorems.example: A fair coin-flip random walk, rescaled, converges to standard Brownian motion.
theorems.examReady: State the sqrt(n) scaling and why it matches variances.

theorems.name: Quadratic Variation of Brownian Motion
theorems.statement: For a partition with mesh \to 0, \sum_k [B(t_{k+1})-B(t_k)]^2 \to T over [0,T].
theorems.intuition: Unlike smooth functions (quadratic variation 0), Brownian motion's roughness gives it positive quadratic variation.
theorems.proofSketch: Each term has expectation \Delta t_k; variance of the sum \to 0 as mesh shrinks.
theorems.example: This positive quadratic variation is exactly why Ito calculus departs from ordinary calculus.
theorems.examReady: E[Q_n]=T exactly for every partition; Var(Q_n)\to0.
